Videocittà is an audiovisual festival held at Rome’s iconic ex-Gasometer, showcasing innovative performances that bridge art, technology, and creativity.

Thanks to our collaboration with the European Institute of Design (I.E.D.), we had the opportunity to design three live performances for this unique event.

Inspired by the venue’s industrial aesthetic and equipped with a high-powered outdoor projector, the performances blended experimental visuals and immersive soundscapes to create a captivating experience for the audience.

The powerful projector and unique outdoor setting elevated the performance, making it a highlight of the festival.

projects.title: Computer Generated Memories
projects.description: A generative and immersive installation that explores memory through digital visuals.
projects.content:
AV Installation
//Computer Generated Memories
2023
Computer Generated Memories, is an audiovisual installation created for the 2024 edition of Charta Festival, exhibited at Fondazione Pastificio Cerere in Rome. The project explores humanity’s disconnection from the natural world, focusing on how daily practices and constructed environments foster an illusion of superiority and control over nature. Through a visually evocative narrative, it invites reflection on the fragility of these constructs.
AudioVisual Performance
1920x1080 | Video full HD Apple ProRes 422
duration: 30'00"
+
CLICK FOR SOUND
General Description*
Computer Generated
Memories
Computer Generated Memories is an audiovisual installation created for the 2024 edition of Charta Festival, exhibited at Fondazione Pastificio Cerere in Rome. Although initially developed for the festival only, the project was later showcased in Anagni, Italy, at the newly restored "Palazzo della Cultura”.

The project explores humanity’s disconnection from the natural world, focusing on how daily practices and constructed environments foster an illusion of superiority and control over nature. Through a visually evocative narrative, it invites reflection on the fragility of these constructs.

Computer Generated
Memories
Developed in TouchDesigner, the installation merges point clouds with curated sound design to create an immersive ambient experience. By visually deconstructing human-altered spaces, the project highlights their inherent vulnerability, presenting a fragmented view of environments shaped by anthropocentric practices.

The result is a contemplative piece that bridges technology and ecology through art.
